idiom_name: instrument(name, payload) / subscribe(name_or_regexp) with subscriber objects
implementation_notes: In Rails the channel is ActiveSupport::Notifications: instrument(name, payload) publishes around a block, subscribe(name_or_regexp) registers a block or callable and returns a subscriber object whose unsubscribe removes it, subscribed(...) scopes the registration to a block, and monotonic_subscribe uses monotonic time for accurate durations. Event objects carry name, duration, allocations and payload, so instrumentation consumers get metrics for free, and matching by regexp lets one subscriber observe a family of events. Outside Rails the standard library's observer module is the object-level alternative.
pitfalls: The framework is built for long-running subscribers: unsubscribing in a hot path wipes internal caches (the documentation warns about it explicitly).
A subscriber exception propagates to the instrumenting code and can break the block's caller.
Subscriptions are global to the process, so a request-scoped subscriber leaks into every later request unless subscribed/unsubscribed scopes it.

variants.name: stdlib observer library (Observable module)
variants.implementation_notes: The observer library that ships with Ruby mixes Observable into the notifying class and provides add_observer/delete_observer/notify_observers with a changed flag; observers are keyed by object and receive the method named at registration (update by default, or :call for callables). It is the per-subject realization: each publisher owns its observer list, so it fits object-level notification and keeps the collaboration local rather than creating a process-wide event namespace. Its documentation notes the pattern is also called publish/subscribe, which makes it the direct predecessor of the Notifications bus.
variants.code_sketch:
require 'observer'

class Ticker
  include Observable

  def update_price(price)
    changed                     # arm the notification
    notify_observers(price)     # publish to every registered observer
  end
end
pitfalls: The observer hash holds strong references, so observers must deregister or the subject keeps them alive.
notify_observers only fires while changed is true - a forgotten changed call silently publishes nothing.
An exception raised inside one observer aborts the remaining notification loop.
